Two Teenagers Die in Fiery Stolen Vehicle Crash in Perth's North-East

02 Nov 2026, 06:31 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily World Desk · Source: www.abc.net.au

2 min read

Incident Overview

Two 16-year-old boys have died following a single-vehicle crash in Bullsbrook, a suburb in Perth's north-east. The incident occurred on Saturday night when a grey BMW 3 Series sedan left the road on Railway Parade, collided with multiple trees, and subsequently caught fire.

Official Findings

Western Australia Police Commissioner Col Blanch confirmed the vehicle involved had been reported stolen prior to the accident. While investigations into the circumstances remain in the early stages, Commissioner Blanch noted that the severity of the wreckage and the vehicle's position suggest speed was likely a contributing factor.

Casualties and Survivors

  • Deceased: Two 16-year-old males.
  • Injured: Two 17-year-old males who were seated in the rear of the vehicle.

The two survivors were transported to Royal Perth Hospital with injuries described by officials as non-life-threatening. Commissioner Blanch remarked on the gravity of the scene, noting that the survivors were fortunate to have escaped the vehicle, which reportedly rolled and caught fire following the collision.

Investigation and Appeals

Major crash investigators are currently examining the site to determine the precise sequence of events. At this stage, WA Police have indicated that it is too early to determine if the surviving passengers will face criminal charges.

How to assist the investigation:

Authorities are requesting assistance from the public to help establish the timeline leading up to the crash. Individuals are encouraged to come forward if they have:

  • Dash-cam footage from the Bullsbrook area on Saturday night.
  • CCTV recordings from nearby residences or businesses.
  • Mobile phone footage or relevant information.

Witnesses are urged to contact Crime Stoppers to provide evidence to the investigation team. Officials emphasized that despite the vehicle being stolen, the loss of life remains a significant tragedy for the community, the affected families, and the first responders who attended the scene.
